name: What to Expect During Your Kitchen Plumbing Upgrade

step.name: Step 1: Initial Consultation & Planning
step.text: This is where you'll discuss your vision, appliance choices, and any relocations or new installations (like a pot filler or instant-hot water unit). A professional will document existing pipe locations and conditions, helping to finalize your cabinet and appliance layout. This phase sets the blueprint for the entire project and can take anywhere from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on design complexity.

step.name: Step 2: Permit Application & Design Finalization
step.text: Once the layout is solid, the design for supply, drain, and shutoff locations is finalized. If you're moving fixtures, adding new lines, or altering drain/vent work, you'll likely need a plumbing permit. Your contractor will guide you through this, handling the application process. This step can take a few weeks as local building departments review plans and issue permits.

step.name: Step 3: Rough-in Plumbing Work
step.text: After permits are secured, the demolition begins (if needed), and the new rough-in plumbing is installed. This involves running new water supply lines, drain-waste-vent piping, and setting up the connections for your sink, dishwasher, and other appliances before walls are closed up. This phase usually lasts several days to a week.

step.name: Step 4: Rough-in Inspection
step.text: Crucially, before any walls or cabinets go in, the rough-in plumbing must pass inspection by the local authority. This ensures everything is up to code and installed correctly. Your contractor will schedule and be present for this. It's a critical checkpoint, typically a short appointment, but requires everything to be exposed.

step.name: Step 5: Fixture Installation & Testing
step.text: Once the walls are closed and cabinets are installed, your new sink, faucet, dishwasher, and other plumbing fixtures are connected. The system is then pressure- and leak-tested thoroughly to catch any issues before they become a problem. This final installation and testing can take a couple of days.

step.name: Step 6: Final Inspection (If Required)
step.text: Finally, where required by your local jurisdiction, a final inspection will be conducted to ensure all finished plumbing work meets code and functions properly. This is the last step before you can fully enjoy your upgraded kitchen.
